learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master the use of Personal, Possessive, and Demonstrative pronouns to make sentences flow better and avoid repeating nouns.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Imagine saying, "Rohan took Rohan's bag to Rohan's house." Sounds funny, right? Pronouns are super-words that rescue us from repeating nouns over and over! 🦸‍♂️

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Personal pronouns take the place of specific people, animals, or things in a sentence. They can be the subject (doing the action) or the object (receiving the action).
examples_or_templates: Subject: I, you, he, she, it, we, they (e.g., She is reading.)
Object: me, you, him, her, it, us, them (e.g., The teacher called him.)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Possessive pronouns show ownership. Unlike possessive adjectives (like 'my' or 'her' which need a noun after them), possessive pronouns stand ALONE.
examples_or_templates: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs
This is my book. ➡️ This book is mine.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Demonstrative pronouns point out specific things. We use 'This' and 'These' for things nearby, and 'That' and 'Those' for things far away.
examples_or_templates: Near: This (singular), These (plural) - 'This is my favorite song.'
Far: That (singular), Those (plural) - 'Are those your shoes over there?'

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which pronoun correctly replaces 'Rita and I'?
❓ Complete the sentence: 'That bicycle belongs to him. It is ______.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the demonstrative pronoun: 'Look at _____ birds flying high in the sky!'
subjective_practice.hint: The birds are plural and far away.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change the sentence to use a possessive pronoun: 'It is our classroom.'
subjective_practice.hint: Move the ownership word to the end: 'The classroom is _______.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Underline the personal pronoun in the objective case: 'My mother baked a cake for me.'
subjective_practice.hint: Who received the cake? Look for the pronoun after the verb/preposition.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🕵️‍♂️ Pronoun Detective
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Read a short paragraph from your favorite storybook. Write down 5 pronouns you find and label whether they are Personal, Possessive, or Demonstrative!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Personal Pronouns (I, them, we) replace nouns as subjects or objects.
⭐ Possessive Pronouns (mine, theirs) show ownership and stand alone without a noun.
⭐ Demonstrative Pronouns (this, that, these, those) point to specific things near or far.
